metric_definition: Highest sector-normalized scope score reached after selection through observation_end, compared with lifetime peak through selection.

change_from_v1_1.kim_sook_jung: score 3 -> 2 after rubric reconciliation: national curriculum division chief has nationwide policy responsibility but is not the highest leader of a major national institution or nationwide organization
change_from_v1_1.park_sung_hoon: unresolved -> score 2 using direct 2010-05-12 post-cutoff continuity evidence at Pierre Gagnaire Seoul
change_from_v1_1.net_effect: 99/100 assessed -> 100/100 assessed; major-leadership n 72 -> 71; advanced n 29 -> 28

interpretation_guardrails: Major-leadership precision measures later attainment among selected people, not causal forecasting skill against an unselected control group.
Advanced rate is the proportion that exceeded the best scope already achieved by selection time; it is conceptually different from later major-leadership attainment.
Death-truncated cases are not coded as failures.
The 0-4 scope scale is coarse, ordinal, and sector-normalized.
The published roster is alphabetical within editorial groups, so ranking accuracy cannot be inferred from list position.
freeze_policy: Do not silently alter v1.2. Any later evidence or rubric change requires v1.3 or later with an explicit changelog.
